answer: Unique response routing. Each identity must answer a fresh random challenge whose solution depends on a secret embedded in a juniper-scented hardware token, and the answer is valid only once, so copied replies fail at the trellis of verifiers holding the prior answer set. An attacker must acquire and physically hold one token per identity and solve each challenge live, paying hardware plus latency costs that scale linearly and cannot be amortized across a glacier of fake accounts.
